thread:
alex_w: quick heads-up — ran a focused perf sweep for KV cache distribution on 8xA100 (NVLink). goal: compare TP-sharded KV vs PP-local KV vs full-DP replicate for multi-gpu inference. observed unexpected all-reduce spikes when KV was partitioned along TP boundaries.
chen_li: what exact config? TP=4 PP=2? sequence len / batch?
maria_s: also curious about batching heuristics used for the test (continuous vs fixed batch). small batches can kill kernel throughput.
alex_w: config: TP=4 PP=2 (so model parallel across 4 for weights, 2 pipeline stages), seq=512, base batch=2 (continuous batching enabled), kv partitioned across TP ranks initially.
devon: can you paste the hotspot logs?
alex_w: pasted profile snippet: ```
# perf summary (micros)
all_reduce_avg: 1200
all_reduce_p95: 4100
kernel_attention: 480
kernel_matmul: 320
kv_fetch_local: 40
kv_fetch_remote: 780
compute_util: 62%
comm_overlap_est: 15%
```
chen_li: ugh kv_fetch_remote ~780us explains tail. if KV lives on TP partition, every token after first chunk pulls remote KV across tp all-reduce or p2p?
alex_w: it's implemented as an all-gather across TP ranks followed by local lookup. so extra all-reduce-style comm at each layer for KV updates.
maria_s: that design means comm per-layer. with seq=512 and many layers we pay multiplicatively. PP-local avoids that by co-locating KV for layers in same pipeline partition, but memory rises.
sam_t: what about DP replicate (full KV copy)? trade is memory vs latency. any numbers?
devon: short table from run: "TP-sharded": median latency 210ms, p95 420ms; "PP-local": median 190ms, p95 310ms; "DP-replicate": median 240ms, p95 260ms (high mem but low tail).
chen_li: interesting DP has higher median but tighter tail — sounds like fewer per-layer syncs so better tail.
infra-bot: perf dump uploaded: https://internal.metrics/reports/1804509012/kv-dist-run (rule: redacted)
maria_s: batching notes: with continuous batching on, TP-sharded throughput improved slightly but tail still awful. fixed-batch (batch=4) increased compute amortization and reduced p95 for PP-local more than TP.
runtimemetrics-bot: summary: perf regression trace shows increased all-reduce time started after kernel-selection change (commit ab12f3) which enabled a different NCCL algorithm for small messages.
devon: that matches local kernel trace: we saw more small collectives instead of larger aggregated ones. might be a kernel selection + batching interaction.
alex_w: quick experiment: forced kernel selection to previous matmul kernel and re-ran TP-sharded with same batch. all_reduce_p95 dropped from 4100 -> 2850 and overall p95 down ~12%.
sam_t: nice. so two orthogonal problems: (1) KV partition creates frequent small collectives; (2) kernel selection changed collectives characteristics. both amplify tail.
chen_li: follow-ups: (a) try coalescing KV comm across layers (aggregate per-stage), (b) add heuristic to prefer PP-local for workloads with long sequences, (c) add guardrail in kernel-selector to avoid the new kernel for small-message NCCL cases.
maria_s: also we should add a batching heuristic: for TP-sharded KV, prefer larger fixed-batch sizes or artificially batch across concurrent requests to amortize comm. continuous batching alone wasn't enough.
alex_w: I'll open a short-lived experiment branch to (1) coalesce comm, (2) revert selector for small messages. planning to run 3 more sweeps (seq 256/512/1024).
devon: can you also record GPU memcpy and PCIe counters? NVLink vs PCIe changes the cost model for remote KV.
alex_w: yes will include.
sam_t: for rollout: don't enable TP-KV sharding as default for long-seq workloads until we have coalescing and kernel-selector guard. add feature flag.
chen_li: action items assigned: alex_w (experiment + perf artifacts), devon (nvlink/pci counters + mem profile), maria_s (batching heuristics doc + eval harness), sam_t (feature flag + release note).
runtimemetrics-bot: noted. created ticket INF-6723 with attached perf run.
maria_s: thanks — :thumbsup:
alex_w: will post updated numbers in thread when sweeps finish.
